 Sharjah's roof took a pounding on Thursday night. Sikandar Raza cleared it with the last ball of Zimbabwe's reply, his ninth six, and still finished 19 runs short.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Afghanistan had been 38 for 5 when Azmatullah Omarzai and Ijaz Ahmad Ahmadzai came together, and the pair added 142, the biggest stand for the sixth wicket or lower in T20Is.
 Omarzai went on to 116 off 50 balls with twelve sixes, before Rashid Khan hit three successive sixes in the final over to make it 221 for 7.
 Rashid also became the first bowler to reach 200 men's T20I wickets. Raza's unbeaten 106 off 56 balls, at 40, made him the oldest man to score a T20I hundred. Afghanistan and Zimbabwe meet again at Sharjah on Sunday at 8pm IST, with the series won 2-0 and Zimbabwe's batters looking for support beyond Raza.
 Afghanistan vs Zimbabwe prediction: Who will win?
 Afghanistan should complete the sweep, and the reason has less to do with Omarzai's fireworks than with how this side survives when things go wrong. They lost four wickets for fewer than 20 runs on Thursday and still won comfortably, which says plenty about the depth and nerve in their dressing room. 
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Zimbabwe's problem is structural. Evans and Matigimu took early wickets and then bled runs when it mattered, and a side with only one proven big hitter cannot keep up with side that has some serious batters.
 The Cricket News Prediction : Afghanistan to win
